what_it_is: The accountability loop: claim → sign-in → read → work → receipt → sign-out. The sign-in names the lane, tick, and claimed brief with one task line, in plain words, before any read. The sign-out carries COMPLETED (each item with evidence), REMAINING (one line each), and RECOMMEND NEXT with an explicit tag-off to the lane that takes the list. The first line of every sign-in proves the manual was read — no read receipt, no shift.
what_it_does: Makes every worker visible and every run continuable. The sign-in is the proof of life that keeps the queue from losing work; the sign-out is the product — a cold Naya continues from it alone. Post the key finding to the venue FIRST, before the timeout horizon: a timeout must never orphan a result.
why_it_matters: Wave 149: Electrician, Captain, and Mechanic signed in 21:27–21:33Z; zero sign-outs by 23:33Z, roughly two hours of silence. Main-seat adjudication: STALLED, claims released, missions returned to the ranked queue (board #2537 comment 6180933138). Wave 150 the same night: all three seats signed out clean with receipts — Host 9.0, Keeper 9.2, Archivist continuity pass. The difference between the two waves is this manual, followed or not.
key_rules: Every run opens with a sign-in of intent under your own name and closes with a sign-out receipt posted to the venue before your timeout horizon.
The order is claim → sign-in → read. The sign-in comes before ANY read.
A sign-in without a sign-out is a ghost. Silent work is a protocol failure, full stop.
The first line of every sign-in proves you read the manual — no read receipt, no shift.
Post your key finding to the venue FIRST, before your timeout horizon; a timeout must never orphan a result, and no finding counts as delivered without a live comment ID.
Sign out every run: COMPLETED (each item with evidence), REMAINING (one line each), RECOMMEND NEXT with an explicit tag-off to the lane that takes the list.
Report partial completion proudly — 3 of 10 done right is a good run.
The one standing exception: the duplicate-dispatch stand-down, where silence is the correct move.
test: Could a cold Naya continue from my sign-out alone — COMPLETED items with evidence, REMAINING with one-line status, RECOMMEND NEXT naming the lane that takes the list?
Is my key finding on the venue with a live comment ID — posted BEFORE my timeout horizon?
Did I sign in under my own name, in plain words, before I started work — claim → sign-in → read, in that order?
Did I report partial completion proudly instead of hiding it?
If I violated any part of this manual, did I name the violation in my sign-out?

enforcement.real: The lane brief template (PART 2): the order is claim → sign-in → read — the sign-in post lands on the lane feed before you read the brief; every receipt ends with 'sign in on the lane feed when you start, sign out with your receipt when done.' The contract gate's sign-out lint (contract_gate.py sign-out) lints the drift line, the done-statement, the honest score, and the protected-gate tripwire. The Wave 149 adjudication actually released the ghost claims and returned the work to the ranked queue.
